questions.prompt: In a spectrum from a prism, which colour is bent the least?
questions.explain: Red has the longest wavelength and bends least.

questions.prompt: Why do stars twinkle but planets usually don’t?
options: Stars are point sources, so atmospheric refraction makes their light flicker
Planets are closer to the Moon

questions.prompt: Why does the sky look dark to astronauts above the atmosphere?
options: The Sun is dimmer in space
There is no air to scatter sunlight

questions.prompt: Where must the Sun be to see a rainbow?
questions.explain: Raindrops refract and reflect sunlight back towards you.

questions.prompt: The beam of sunlight entering a dusty room is visible because of…
questions.explain: Dust particles scatter light sideways into your eyes.

questions.prompt: Which colour of light is scattered most by air molecules?
Explain why the Sun looks reddish at sunrise and sunset but white-yellow at noon.
questions.modelAnswer: At sunrise and sunset, sunlight passes through a much longer path of atmosphere to reach us. Along the way, most of the shorter wavelengths (blue, violet) are scattered out of the beam by air molecules. The light that reaches us is mainly the longer, less-scattered wavelengths (red, orange). At noon the path is short, so little is scattered and the Sun looks white-yellow.
rubric: Longer path through air at sunrise/sunset
